claim: Tether: chance one 5 ms scan hears the child's band
note: A 5 ms window every 5 s almost never coincides with an advertisement sent every 800 ms: four scans in a row all miss 98% of the time with the child beside the parent. A window of 811 ms cannot miss; it costs 746 uA.

claim: Tether: separation at which the alert sounds
note: Losing the signal happens at the edge of radio range, not at 25-30 m. To alert at 30 m the parent tag must treat an RSSI below about -78 dBm as a miss.

claim: Transmit time per advertisement on Coded PHY
note: 1.25 ms fits a 1M PHY event. On Coded PHY S=8 the same 15 bytes take 5.95 ms, which gives 12.8 months at 25 C and 9.0 months at -5 C.

claim: Supply during an unbuffered buzzer pulse at -5 C
Supply during the pulse with the 100 uF capacitor
note: 100 uF behind 42 ohm has a time constant of 4.2 ms, far shorter than the 100 ms pulse, so it does not hold the supply up. Either the capacitor must be at least 895 uF or the pulse current at most 29.8 mA.

claim: Chance of forging an SOS in one try
Chance of forging a wake token in one try
Pseudonyms are unique in the lookup table
note: With 10,000 tags and a three-slot window, two entries share a 32-bit pseudonym about one time in ten. The table therefore maps a pseudonym to a list and separates clashes by the slot counter.

claim: Replayed frames are rejected
note: Arrival tuples carry no MIC and poles hold no keys, so a frame replayed at another pole within its own slot window (up to 45 minutes) is accepted as a sighting. Only SOS frames are fully verified.

claim: Bloom heartbeat false-positive rate
note: 64 bytes hold about 78 wearables at a 5% error rate. Dense hub poles are on fibre and can send a larger filter.

claim: Pole spacing on the LoRa tracks
note: 195 poles over 21.0 km of track is one pole per 108 m. Still inside the Coded PHY range of Eq. 2.

claim: Wearable transmit power on the nRF52811
note: The nRF52811 is specified up to +4 dBm. +8 dBm needs a part such as the nRF52820 or nRF52833. To be confirmed against the datasheet before the bill of materials is fixed.

claim: SOS reaches the control room within 4 s (3,000-tag surge)
note: Simulation. The first LoRa attempt is lost 23% of the time under the surge, and a repeat waits an assumed 3 s. On fibre poles every SOS arrives in under a second.
